newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Shum Yip shrs in strong demand -analysts.
newsitem.headline: Shum Yip shrs in strong demand -analysts.

text.p: Demand for Shum Yip Investment Ltd shares is running high and the stock looks set for a strong debut after the red chip company said this week its Hong Kong public offering was 438 times subscribed, analysts said on Wednesday.
Shum Yip shares are set to start trading on Friday and brokers said the stock was quoted at HK$2.70 to HK$3.00 in the grey market, well above its offer price of HK$1.85.
"Investor enthusiasm for red chip IPOs (initial public offerings) has calmed down slightly but Shum Yip shares look sustainable," said Pamela Lam at Pacific Challenge Securities.
She said the heavy over-subscription level, the highest this year, helped sentiment.

The property development and investment company, which is backed by the Shenzhen municipal government, received applications for a total 29.54 billion shares compared with 67.5 million new shares offered.
"I don't think the share could hold above HK$3.00," said an analyst at a regional brokerage house.
But he said the size of this issue was relatively small and the share price could be easily boosted by speculators.
Analysts said Shum Yip might undergo short-term profit-taking if the share rises too sharply on its first day.

But they said the medium to long-term outlook for the company was positive with the parent company expected to inject additional development projects into the company and property prices in the Shenzhen market believed to have bottomed out.
The parent company Shum Yip Holdings holds about 63 percent of the company following the IPO.
